title: Proteomics
intro: Describe your samples and comparisons; the page writes the lab-proteomics commands, in order, for you to copy into a terminal on the cluster. Nothing you type leaves your browser.

samples.intro: The label of each sample is the name of its intensity column in the protein table, and experimental_design.csv (label, condition, replicate) maps each label to its group. Paste the table's header line or the intensity column names in section 2 to fill the labels, drop an existing experimental_design.csv, or type them.

listing.note: The column names pasted in section 2 fill this table (one row per intensity column); edit any cell.

fields.label: I have not installed the pipelines yet
Project folder
fields.hint: init creates it. Use an absolute path: the config's file paths are read by the cluster jobs.

fields.label: Project name (optional)
fields.hint: init --name; empty uses the folder's name.

fields.label: Protein table
fields.hint: Absolute path to the MaxQuant or Proteome Discoverer export (input.protein_data). lab-proteomics reads the columns Accession and Description (or Symbol) and every column whose name contains an underscore as an intensity column: keep one intensity family (for example LFQ) in the table.

fields.label: Intensity column names
fields.hint: Paste the table's header line (tab-separated) or the intensity column names, one per line. The LFQ intensity / Intensity / iBAQ columns become the labels; other columns are ignored.

fields.label: Imputation method
fields.hint: GSimp, MinProb: missing-not-at-random (low abundance). knn, bpca, RF: missing at random. knn_GSimp and bpca_MinProb mix the two (MAR_MNAR).

fields.label: Significance column
fields.hint: With pvalue the calls use the raw p-value cutoff; both columns are always written to the tables.

fields.label: Adjusted p threshold
fields.hint: Pipeline default 0.1; written only when changed.

fields.label: p-value threshold
fields.hint: Pipeline default 0.05; written only when changed.

fields.label: log2 fold-change threshold
fields.hint: Pipeline default 0.6; written only when changed.

sections.title: Advanced (optional)
sections.summary: FDR method, Slurm account and partition, run name, a dry run only. Empty or unchanged fields change nothing.

fields.label: Run name
fields.hint: Names the folder under results/; empty names it after the comparisons.

fields.label: Dry run only: write the job scripts, submit nothing

session.comment: Every session: activate the lab environment

lines.comment: init writes inputs/project_config.yaml, a header-only experimental_design.csv and a header-only contrasts.csv.

blocks.title: write the experimental design (label, condition, replicate)

lines.comment: Paste the protein table's header line or its intensity column names in section 2, or add rows in section 3: this step then writes inputs/experimental_design.csv for you.
label must match the intensity column names of the protein table exactly; condition is the group.
Add comparisons in section 3: this step then writes inputs/contrasts.csv. Until then it is header-only and analyze stops with 'No valid contrasts found'.

blocks.title: point the config at your data and settings

lines.comment: lab-proteomics has no `config set`: this edits inputs/project_config.yaml in place (comments kept; a missing key is added to its section).
It also sets project.name (the project name above, else the folder's name): init leaves the example's name in the config.

bodyText: shown = value if re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+', value) else "'" + value.replace("'", "''") + "'"
start = next((i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if re.match(section + r':\s*(#.*)?$', l)), None)
end = next((j for j in range(start + 1, len(lines)) if lines[j] and not lines[j].startswith((' ', '\t', '#'))), len(lines))
lines[j] = m.group(1) + key + ': ' + shown + ('   ' + m.group(2) if m.group(2) else '')

lines.comment: check may warn that the experimental design has no sample column: it looks for sample, while proteomics uses label. The warning is harmless.

blocks.title: run the analysis (dry run first, then submit)

lines.comment: Dry run only: the job scripts are written under results/, nothing is submitted. Untick the dry run to get the submit, status and report lines.

blocks.title: wait for the jobs, then write the report

lines.comment: Repeat status until every contrast shows a result; report then reads the newest run (or the one named by --run-name).
